items.title: NextAuth JWT session never re-validates against the backend, so a demoted/deactivated user keeps full old-role access for up to 30 days
items.body:
## Impact

When an admin changes a user's role (UserService.setRole), deactivates them, or removes a tenant membership, none of that invalidates the user's already-issued browser session. Because the session strategy is JWT with no server-side lookup, and the web proxy blindly forwards whatever role/tenant is baked into that token, the affected user continues to authenticate with their OLD role and OLD tenant scope for up to 30 days (the default maxAge) or until they happen to log out. In a property-management SaaS this means a demoted PROPERTY_MANAGER or an offboarded TENANT_ADMIN retains full prior access -- including financial screens -- long after an admin believes access was revoked.

## Evidence

- `web/src/auth.ts:71-90` — jwt() callback only copies role/tenantId/tenantIds onto the token when `user` is present, i.e. at initial sign-in; on every subsequent request the token is returned unchanged. session() callback just projects the (unrefreshed) token onto session.user.
- `web/src/auth.ts:102-104` — `session: { strategy: 'jwt' }` with no `maxAge` override -> NextAuth's 30-day default JWT lifetime; no `.env.local`/config sets NEXTAUTH session maxAge.
- `web/src/proxy.ts:73-75` — X-User-Id / X-User-Role / X-User-Tenant-Id sent to the backend on every proxied call are read straight from the (never-refreshed) token, not re-checked against current user state.
- `backend/src/main/java/com/datagami/rentaxis/core/security/ApiSecurityFilter.java:94-155` — Legacy header path (the one the web proxy always uses) does no per-request DB lookup of the user's current role/status -- it trusts the headers as presented, so a stale token's role/tenant keep working unconditionally.

## Recommendation

Either shorten the JWT maxAge substantially and/or implement a revocation check: on each proxied request (or periodically via NextAuth's `session.update()`/JWT refresh hook), re-fetch the user's current role/status from the backend and force sign-out if it no longer matches the token, or move to a database session strategy that can be invalidated server-side on role/status change.

## Open questions

- Whether AuthTokenService (the backend's separate Bearer-token path) is enabled in production and used by any other client; if so the same staleness likely applies there too, but that is outside web/src.

---

**Severity:** high · **Confidence:** confirmed · **Effort:** M · **Score:** 9  
**Lens:** web

items.title: AAP-85842 Disable reverse RBAC sync during JWT claims old Role sync
items.body:
## Summary

- Wraps `_sync_old_rbac` in `disable_rbac_sync()` alongside the existing `disable_activity_stream()`
- Each `members.add()` was firing `m2m_changed` → `sync_members_to_new_rbac` → serial `give_permission` with full RBAC recompute, negating the bulk speedup from AAP-85067
- This is safe because `save_user_claims` already created all DAB assignments via `bulk_give_permissions`; `members.add()` only needs to populate the old `Role.members` M2M table

**Benchmark (550 grants, AWX sqlite):**

| Metric | Before | After | Improvement |
|--------|--------|-------|-------------|
| Total time | 19.16s | 2.17s | 8.8x |
| Old RBAC sync | 17.76s | 0.75s | 23.7x |

## Test plan

- [ ] Existing `test_app/tests/rbac/` suite passes
- [ ] AWX JWT consumer tests pass
- [ ] Perfscale verification with 500+ grants shows acceptable timing

items.title: Security: Plaintext secrets in server/.env (current + old agent key, AGENT_SECRET, Supabase service role, Privy JWT key)
items.body:
## Criticality

🔴 Critical. Disk/backup/container/cache/editor-history access to a single plaintext file = full system control: co-sign pending txs for every user (agent is owner on every Safe), forge Privy tokens, bypass Supabase RLS, drain treasury.

## Where

- `server/.env` (gitignored but on-disk, contains live prod secrets)
- History implies prior commit/rotation (commented '# OLD AGENT SIGNER PRIVATE KEY' with a prior key value)

## What's in the file

- `AGENT_PRIVATE_KEY` (current, used as Safe co-signer AND relayer)
- An **old commented-out** `AGENT_PRIVATE_KEY` whose address is likely still an owner on Safes that never re-swapped
- `AGENT_SECRET` (agent→server bearer — single shared, no per-user scope)
- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` (bypasses all RLS)
- `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` + commented-out old
- `PRIVY_JWT_VERIFICATION_KEY` (lets anyone forge Privy identity tokens for this app)
- `SAFE_API_KEY`, `TREASURY_PRIVATE_KEY`, `RESEND_API_KEY`, `PIMLICO_API_KEY`, `LIFI_API_KEY`, `ZERION_API_KEY`, RPC URLs

## Remediation

1. Rotate **every** secret currently in the file. Move secrets to a secret manager (Vault / Doppler / AWS Secrets Manager / Supabase Vault). Never commit plaintext.
2. Treat the current and old `AGENT_PRIVATE_KEY` as fully compromised. Audit onchain owner-sets across all Safes: any Safe still carrying the old agent address → run `swapOwner` (or force `protected → detached → re-guarded`) to revoke. Audit script: `pnpm --filter zhentan-server safe:verify-derivations` plus an owner-set sweep.
3. Treat `PRIVY_JWT_VERIFICATION_KEY` as compromised — rotate via Privy dashboard; consider all existing tokens invalid until expiry.
4. Rotate `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` in the Supabase dashboard; prefer anon-key + RLS where possible.
5. Treat `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` as compromised — revoke-and-reissue via BotFather. Same for `SAFE_API_KEY` (developer.safe.global), Resend, Pimlico, LiFi, Zerion, treasury key.
6. Add a CI/git-history scan (e.g. gitleaks) and a pre-commit hook. Confirm no historical commits contain `.env`.

## Related

- Tracks the structural "hosted signing key is also relayer key" concern (see separate issue).
- Enables the cross-user execute path.

items.title: fix(shared,backend): Allow for old org_role format in JWT v1 where `org:` is missing
items.body:
## Description
Bug fix: In `createCheckAuthorization` allow for old `org_role` format in JWT v1 where `org:` is missing.

Example session claims:
```json
{
  "org_id": "org_xxxx",
  "org_permissions": [],
  "org_role": "admin",
  "org_slug": "test"
}
```
Code
```ts
authObject.has({ role: 'org:admin' }) // -> true
authObject.has({ role: 'admin' }) // -> true
```
